Create a template yaml file for supplying factor metadata for a data object that cannot be read into R

write_other_factors.Rd

write_other_factors creates a template as a yaml file for supplying the codes and definitions of categorical attributes of an otherEntity (e.g., a zip file of LiDAR point clouds in LAZ format) that cannot be read into the R environment.

Usage

write_other_factors(
  target_file,
  factors,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  metadata_path = NULL
)

Arguments

target_file

(character) The quoted name of the data file (e.g., "lidar_tiles.zip"). The file is used only to name the template; it does not need to be readable.

factors

(list) A named list in which each name is a categorical attribute and each element is a character vector of the codes of that attribute; use character(0) if the codes are not yet known.

overwrite

(logical) Logical indicating if an existing factors file in the target directory should be overwritten.

metadata_path

(character) Directory to which the template is written. Defaults to metadata_path in config.yaml, else the working directory.

Value

The path to the template is returned invisibly, and a template for providing code definitions is written to metadata_path.

Details

The template is named for the target file without its extension (e.g., lidar_tiles.zip yields lidar_tiles_factors.yaml) and written to metadata_path. Each attribute of class factor in the attributes template (see write_other_attributes) must have an entry in the factors template, and every code requires a definition. Codes that are not known when the template is created are written as a single blank level to be completed (add further levels as needed). If a factors template is provided without an attributes template, create_otherEntity documents a single attribute using the entity_value_description argument (e.g., the value classes of a raster).

When to use

Attributes describe variables or fields that exist within the data object, such as the point record fields (e.g., X, Y, Z, Classification) of LiDAR point clouds in a zip file, the attribute table of a zipped shapefile, the value classes of a raster, or the columns of spreadsheets in a zip file. Each attribute must correspond to a variable in the object.

What is not allowed

Attributes are not a place for metadata about the file itself (e.g., author, number of files in an archive, version, software used to create it); provide those details in the description or additional_information arguments of create_otherEntity, the methods, or dataset-level metadata. Do not invent attributes that do not exist in the object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

 # LAS classification codes of the LiDAR point clouds (LAZ) in a zip file;
 # use character(0) for a factor whose codes are not yet known

 capeml::write_other_factors(
   target_file = "lidar_tiles.zip",
   factors     = list(
     Classification = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "17")
   )
 )

} # }
